source_name: LEGISLATIONLINE (OSCE/ODIHR) — North Macedonia country page
why_relevant: OSCE/ODIHR repository of national legislation in English translation, including the Constitution and criminal/AML-adjacent statutes. Where an English rendering of a MK statute exists, this is a defensible, attributable one — helpful for briefing non-MK-reading stakeholders. Coverage of financial-sector statutes is likely partial and translations are unofficial.

source_name: Собрание на РСМ — English-language site (Assembly, EN)
why_relevant: English mirror of the Assembly site covering the Constitution, structure and some legislative material. Lower fidelity and slower than the mk pages, but useful for entity-name normalisation (official English renderings of committee and act names) so that mk and en records can be joined.

source_name: Портал на Министерството за дигитална трансформација / mdt.gov.mk — compilations of financial-system laws
why_relevant: Surfaced hosting a compiled document titled 'закони кои го регулираат финансискиот систем', i.e. a cross-institution list of the statutes in this cell's scope. Marginal but occasionally holds compilations not published elsewhere; a snowball target rather than a monitoring target.

source_name: УФР — Индикатори за субјекти (suspicious-transaction indicator lists per obliged-entity type)
why_relevant: Per-sector indicator lists (banks, exchange offices, fast-money-transfer agents, etc.) are the operational AML rulebook obliged entities must embed in transaction-monitoring systems; updates trigger system-change projects with deadlines.

source_name: УФР — Подзаконски акти (subordinate acts) and Упатства (instructions)
why_relevant: Rulebooks and instructions set reporting formats, thresholds and transposition deadlines for AML reporting by banks and payment providers.

source_name: УФР — Надзор и преземени мерки (supervision & enforcement actions)
why_relevant: Reveals enforcement intensity and which obliged-entity categories are under pressure — a leading indicator of compliance spend by banks and payment operators.

source_name: УФР — Национална процена на ризик / стратегии / акциски планови
why_relevant: The National Risk Assessment and AML strategy/action plans name forthcoming obligations and target dates (e.g. beneficial-ownership, virtual assets, cash thresholds) months before they become law.

source_name: УФР — Reporting portal for obliged entities (АСК/restricted platform)
why_relevant: The existence and technology of the mandated e-reporting channel (login gateway ws-askmk.ufr.gov.mk) tells us the integration surface banks and payment firms must build against; onboarding notices and format changes appear around it.

source_name: Агенција за заштита на личните податоци (АЗЛП) — Personal Data Protection Agency
why_relevant: MK's GDPR-equivalent authority. Its guidance for контролори, opinions and supervisory findings bind banks, card processors and fintechs (biometrics, KYC data retention, cloud, video surveillance at branches/ATMs).

source_name: АЗЛП — Насоки и теми за контролори (controller guidance & thematic pages)
why_relevant: Sector guidance is where practical obligations for financial controllers (DPO appointment, DPIA, transfers, retention) are spelled out; changes here drive bank compliance projects.

source_name: АЗЛП — English site
why_relevant: English mirror provides translated mission/regulatory material useful for cross-checking mk terminology and for reporting to non-MK stakeholders; coverage is likely partial.

source_name: Комисија за хартии од вредност (КХВ) — Securities and Exchange Commission of RNM
why_relevant: Independent regulator for securities, investment funds and takeovers; licences brokerage houses and imposes disclosure/AML obligations on bank-affiliated brokers and custodians.

source_name: КХВ — Регулатива (laws, rulebooks, consolidated texts)
why_relevant: Single page aggregating securities-market rulebooks and consolidated laws; the practical entry point for tracking capital-market rule changes and their entry-into-force dates.

source_name: АСО — Одлуки (decisions) category feed
why_relevant: Chronological stream of adopted decisions — the cleanest machine-readable trail of new insurance-sector obligations and their effective dates.

source_name: УЈП — main site (news, notices, enforcement campaigns)
why_relevant: UJP notices announce fiscalisation control campaigns, deadlines for taxpayers to install/upgrade fiscal devices, and e-service changes — operationally decisive for POS/fiscal vendors and acquirers.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — УФР/УСППФТ institutional page
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is the parent of both УФР and УЈП and the proposer of AML and fiscalisation legislation; its ministry pages point to the responsible units and to draft laws before they reach ENER or the Gazette.

source_name: European Commission — Enlargement: North Macedonia country page (annual Country Reports)
why_relevant: Annual EC Country Report is the single most authoritative external assessment of MK's alignment; Chapter 9 (Financial services), Chapter 4 (Free movement of capital) and Chapter 28 (consumer/financial consumer protection) sections state what MK has transposed, what is missing and the expected next steps, in English, before domestic sources summarise it.

source_name: EC Screening report — North Macedonia, Cluster 3 (Competitiveness and Inclusive Growth, incl. Ch.9 Financial services)
why_relevant: The screening report is the most granular EU-side statement of MK's acquis gaps per chapter: it records MK's own presentation, the Commission's assessment and the level of preparedness, effectively a to-do list of directives/regulations still to be transposed (CRR/CRD, Solvency II, PSD2, DGS, MiFID II, etc.).

source_name: EC Enlargement — news / press releases on North Macedonia
why_relevant: Fastest EU-side signal of regulatory milestones (e.g. the Commission's welcome of MK's inclusion in SEPA, screening completion, Reform Agenda approvals); each item points to the underlying decision document.

source_name: European Payments Council — North Macedonia SEPA scheme participation (news & insights)
why_relevant: EPC is the gatekeeper for SEPA scheme geographical scope; its decisions, criteria and legal-opinion requirements define the concrete compliance bar (PSD2/PAD/IFR/SEPA Regulation transposition) MK PSPs must meet, plus the register of which MK institutions have actually joined SCT/SCT Inst.

source_name: European Banking Authority — North Macedonia equivalence assessment & opinions
why_relevant: EBA's equivalence annex for North Macedonia is a directive-by-directive comparison of MK banking supervision against CRR/CRD, i.e. an EU-authored gap analysis of MK prudential regulation; the underlying Commission equivalence decision has direct legal effect for EU banks' exposures to MK.

source_name: EBA Memorandum of Cooperation with South-Eastern European supervisors (Vienna Initiative)
why_relevant: Sets out the commitment of the MK national bank to align regulatory/supervisory standards with EU ones on an agreed timetable — a durable structural driver of MK rulemaking and a pointer to the Vienna Initiative workstream.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — Memoranda of Understanding (incl. ECB–NBRM MoU)
why_relevant: The ECB/SSM–National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia MoU governs supervisory information exchange over EU banking groups' MK subsidiaries; new or updated MoUs signal deepening integration of MK supervision into the SSM orbit ahead of accession.

source_name: Ministry of European Affairs of North Macedonia (МЕП, ex-СЕП) — EU integration / EC report section
why_relevant: The MK negotiating structure's own hub: Macedonian translations of EC reports, NPAA (National Programme for Adoption of the Acquis) versions, negotiating working-group information for Chapter 9/4, twinning programming. States the domestic transposition calendar in local language.

source_name: NPAA (Национална програма за усвојување на правото на ЕУ) — line-ministry mirrors
why_relevant: The NPAA is the binding national transposition plan: it lists, per chapter, which EU acts will be transposed by which national law and in which quarter — the richest single source of MK regulatory deadlines. Line ministries mirror the chapters relevant to them, which sometimes exposes annexes not visible on the central portal.
